title: 335. It's okay to change your mind

sentences.en: This is an iHeart Podcast, Guaranteed Human.
sentences.zh: 这是一个iHeart播客，保证由真人制作。

sentences.en: I've been really trying to prioritize my health in a realistic way this year, and something that has kept me really motivated is my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 今年我一直在努力以一种现实的方式优先考虑我的健康，而让我保持动力的一个东西就是我的WHOOP。

sentences.en: I am such a data person, which is why I love WHOOP, because I can genuinely see why my body feels differently depending on the day, why I'm running differently,
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常看重数据的人，这就是我喜欢WHOOP的原因，因为我可以真正看出为什么我的身体在不同日子里感觉不同，为什么我的跑步状态不同，

sentences.en: why I'm maybe less focused.
sentences.zh: 为什么我有时注意力不集中。

sentences.en: WHOOP effortlessly tracks my sleep, it tracks my strain, my recovery, my stress, and most importantly, my overall health.
sentences.zh: WHOOP可以轻松追踪我的睡眠、身体压力、恢复情况、压力水平，最重要的是，我的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供了所有这些数据和模式，让我可以做出更好的决定，包括知道什么时候该放松，什么时候该努力。

sentences.zh: 新用户可以在订阅会员之前，先通过30天免费试用体验WHOOP。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 访问join.whoop.com/psychology即可获得一个月的免费WHOOP体验。

sentences.zh: 你有什么绝对不会扔掉的珍贵物品吗？

sentences.zh: 一张电影票、一张登机牌，或者其他对别人来说毫无意义但对你却意义非凡的东西。

sentences.zh: 在新的播客节目《Charmed, with Sam Todd》中，

sentences.en: Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who you are.
sentences.zh: Sam探索了那些成为你生命一部分的记忆、执念和微小的宝藏。

sentences.en: Charmed is warm, it's funny, it's nostalgic, and just full of the little moments and memories that make life matter.
sentences.zh: 《Charmed》温暖、有趣、充满怀旧感，满载着那些让生活变得有意义的点滴瞬间和回忆。

sentences.en: Charmed, with Sam Todd, stories worn to tell with Pandora.
sentences.zh: 《Charmed, with Sam Todd》，与Pandora共同讲述那些值得铭记的故事。

sentences.en: Listen now on iHeart.
sentences.zh: 现在就在iHeart上收听吧。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《20多岁的心理学》，在这个播客里，我们探讨20多岁时会遇到的一些重大人生变化和过渡，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要继续剖析20多岁的心理。

sentences.en: Today, we are talking about decision-making, but not in a way that you expect.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要谈谈决策，但不是你预想的那种方式。

sentences.en: We're not talking about how we can make decisions, how we know that we're making the right decision.
sentences.zh: 我们不是在谈论如何做决定，或者如何知道自己做的是正确的决定。

sentences.en: We're not going to talk about how to weigh up costs and benefits, how to have certainty in your decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们不会谈论如何权衡利弊，或者如何在决策中获得确定性。

sentences.en: We're actually going to talk about the aftermath of making a choice where you realize,
sentences.zh: 我们实际上要谈论的是当你做出选择后，意识到：

sentences.en: hey, this actually isn't right for me.
sentences.zh: 嘿，这其实并不适合我。

sentences.en: This actually isn't what I believe in.
sentences.zh: 这其实并不是我所信仰的。

sentences.en: This actually isn't what I want for my life and why it feels so hard in those moments to admit that we were wrong or, I guess, to change our mind.
sentences.zh: 这其实不是我想要的生活，以及为什么在那些时刻承认我们错了，或者说改变主意，会让人感到如此艰难。

sentences.en: I, obviously, on this podcast, reflect so much on my own personal growth.
sentences.zh: 显然，在这个播客中，我经常反思自己的个人成长。

sentences.en: If you've been here for a long time, you will know that I started the psychology of your 20s basically as a way to kind of therapize myself
sentences.zh: 如果你关注我很久了，你就会知道，我创办《20多岁的心理学》基本上是为了给自己做心理治疗，

sentences.en: and to kind of interrogate, explore, research the stuff that was going on in my own life and in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 去审视、探索和研究我生活中以及20多岁时所经历的事情。

sentences.en: And a big thing that I am learning right now is exactly this.
sentences.zh: 而我现在正在学习的一个重要课题正是这一点。

sentences.en: Changing your mind and having to tell people that or having to let people down is incredibly uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 改变主意并不得不告诉别人，或者不得不让别人失望，是非常令人不舒服的。

sentences.en: It is also absolutely necessary, especially in this decade.
sentences.zh: 但这也是绝对必要的，尤其是在这个十年里。

sentences.en: And I have had to do this a lot recently.
sentences.zh: 最近我不得不经常这样做。

sentences.en: I had to turn down like a really big business opportunity that I really wanted to do, but realized like, you know, no, I'm not right for this or it's not the right time for me.
sentences.zh: 我不得不拒绝一个我非常想做的重大商业机会，但我意识到，不，我不适合这个，或者现在不是合适的时机。

sentences.en: I've changed my mind on some of my political opinions recently.
sentences.zh: 最近我也改变了一些政治观点。

sentences.en: But what really inspired me to talk about this and what has made me realize why we need to talk about this more was a friend of mine who recently called off an engagement
sentences.zh: 但真正启发我谈论这个话题，并让我意识到为什么我们需要更多地讨论它，是因为我的一位朋友最近取消了订婚，

sentences.en: and she's given me permission to talk about this.
sentences.zh: 她允许我谈论这件事。

sentences.en: But basically she knew when she said yes to her now ex-fiancé, like in the bottom of her heart, that this wasn't right.
sentences.zh: 基本上，当她答应她现在的前未婚夫时，她内心深处就知道这并不合适。

sentences.en: And she ignored it for months.
sentences.zh: 但她忽视了这种感觉好几个月。

sentences.en: They'd been together for four years.
sentences.zh: 他们在一起四年了。

sentences.en: Her whole family loved him.
sentences.zh: 她全家人都很喜欢他。

sentences.en: Everyone said they were soulmates.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说他们是灵魂伴侣。

sentences.en: But the relationship obviously looked very different from within, which, you know, as a friend, you only really find out later on most of the time.
sentences.zh: 但从内部看，这段关系显然非常不同，你知道，作为朋友，大多数时候你只能事后才发现。

sentences.en: And she was telling me in hindsight how she was going back and forth, kind of plagued with guilt, plagued with doubt, plagued with this fear of disappointing people,
sentences.zh: 她事后告诉我，她当时是如何反复纠结，被内疚感折磨，被怀疑折磨，被害怕让别人失望的恐惧折磨，

sentences.en: people who had kind of come to expect something from her in any way, something from her relationship.
sentences.zh: 那些以某种方式对她抱有期望的人，或者对她的关系抱有期望的人。

sentences.en: And finally, she just had to make the call.
sentences.zh: 最后，她不得不做出决定。

sentences.en: Obviously, in the aftermath, we've been talking a lot about not like how this happened, but yeah, how did this happen?
sentences.zh: 显然，事后我们一直在谈论的不是这件事是如何发生的，而是，是的，这到底是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: How was it that she ended up engaged to someone who she knew wasn't right for her?
sentences.zh: 为什么她最终会和一个她明知不适合自己的人订婚？

sentences.en: And we've been talking a lot about this whole concept of having to admit to ourselves and having to admit to others that we have changed as a person, that we have changed our minds
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论这个概念，即不得不向自己承认，也不得不向他人承认我们已经改变了，我们已经改变了主意，

sentences.en: and how if we talked about how truly normal this is, we would be saving people a lot of doubt, a lot of heartbreak and a lot of kind of wasted time at the end of the day,
sentences.zh: 如果我们谈论这是多么正常的一件事，我们就能让人们少受很多怀疑、少受很多心碎，少浪费很多时间，

sentences.en: if time can ever be wasted, but that's another discussion.
sentences.zh: 如果时间真的可以被浪费的话，但那是另一个话题了。

sentences.en: So to get into it, this is a quick summary of what we are going to discuss.
sentences.zh: 所以，进入正题，这是我们要讨论内容的简要总结。

sentences.en: First, I want to talk about why we resist changing our minds because of a fear of being judged, a fear of disappointing people, especially our parents.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想谈谈为什么我们因为害怕被评判、害怕让别人失望（尤其是我们的父母）而抗拒改变主意。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about sunk cost fallacy and what it actually means and what it feels like and what comes after disappointment.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论沉没成本谬误，它到底意味着什么，感觉如何，以及失望之后会发生什么。

sentences.en: Secondly, we're going to talk about the cost of staying loyal to old and outdated versions of ourselves and why actually being less afraid to say I was wrong,
sentences.zh: 其次，我们将谈论忠于旧的、过时的自我所付出的代价，以及为什么实际上少一点害怕说“我错了”、

sentences.en: I made the wrong decision, this is not right for me, would actually counterintuitively allow us to make decisions easier and with a lot less anxiety.
sentences.zh: “我做出了错误的决定”、“这不适合我”，反而会让我们更容易做出决定，并减少很多焦虑。

sentences.en: It's a big topic, guys, but honestly, I think there's a lot of clarity that comes with accepting this huge truth.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的话题，伙计们，但老实说，我认为接受这个巨大的真相会带来很多清晰的认识。

sentences.en: You can't always make the right decision, but you cannot make a better one unless you have the courage to admit I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 你不可能总是做出正确的决定，但除非你有勇气承认“我错了”，否则你永远无法做出更好的决定。

sentences.en: And so hopefully this episode gives you the courage.
sentences.zh: 希望这一期节目能给你勇气。

sentences.en: Without further ado, let's get into why it is okay to change your mind.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们进入为什么改变主意是可以的。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: So I know I've kind of framed this discussion as changing your mind about big decisions, like an engagement or, I don't know, a job, but honestly, I think that this extends
sentences.zh: 我知道我把这次讨论设定为关于重大决策的改变主意，比如订婚，或者，我不知道，一份工作，但老实说，我认为这延伸到

sentences.en: to just about anything.
sentences.zh: 几乎任何事情。

sentences.en: Changing your mind about your beliefs, your political opinions, the kind of people you want to surround yourself with, the kind of clothes you want to wear, where you want to live,
sentences.zh: 改变你对信仰、政治观点、你想与之交往的人、你想穿的衣服、你想住的地方、

sentences.en: who you want to be with, what kind of person you see yourself as.
sentences.zh: 你想和谁在一起、你如何看待自己这类事情的看法。

sentences.en: Like there are countless moments and forks in the road where we make choices and we change our mind about who we want to be, either consciously or unconsciously.
sentences.zh: 就像人生中有无数的时刻和岔路口，我们做出选择，然后改变主意，决定自己想成为什么样的人，无论是有意识还是无意识的。

sentences.en: None of these things are ever set in stone just because they were once important to you or because you once claimed it was something that you believed in.
sentences.zh: 这些事情从来都不是一成不变的，仅仅因为它们曾经对你很重要，或者因为你曾经声称那是你所信仰的。

sentences.en: You are allowed to change as a person.
sentences.zh: 你有权作为一个个体去改变。

sentences.en: When you really interrogate this as well, oftentimes some of the core pillars of our identity that we feel most loyal to, some of our core opinions and beliefs
sentences.zh: 当你真正审视这一点时，通常我们最忠诚的一些核心身份支柱，我们的一些核心观点和信仰，

sentences.en: are things that we first started to believe in at like 18 or maybe even younger.
sentences.zh: 往往是我们18岁甚至更年轻时开始相信的东西。

sentences.en: It was often things that were influenced by family, influenced by the people around us, by our environments and the influence of these factors
sentences.zh: 这通常是受家庭、周围的人、环境影响的结果，而这些因素的影响力

sentences.en: kind of diminishes when we leave those spaces and the older we get.
sentences.zh: 在我们离开那些环境以及随着年龄增长时会逐渐减弱。

sentences.en: And we also importantly start to really independently rethink parts of our lives that we've kind of always just assumed or we've kind of just taken for granted
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是，我们开始真正独立地重新思考我们生活中那些一直以来被视为理所当然的部分，

sentences.en: or, you know, decisions that we just felt were inevitable because someone had wanted them from us.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，那些我们觉得不可避免的决定，仅仅因为有人希望我们那样做。

sentences.en: Someone had served it up on a silver platter and said, this is what we've chosen for you.
sentences.zh: 有人把它放在银盘上端给你，说：“这是我们为你选择的。”

sentences.en: Now, changing your mind about those things,
sentences.zh: 现在，改变对这些事情的看法，

sentences.en: terrifying, scary, also a good thing.
sentences.zh: 虽然可怕，但也绝对是一件好事。

sentences.en: This is what we call individuation.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的“个体化”。

sentences.en: It is an essential part of our psychological development whereby we separate from the collective or the norms that have previously shaped us
sentences.zh: 这是我们心理发展中至关重要的一部分，通过它，我们从之前塑造我们的集体或规范中分离出来，

sentences.en: so that we can carve out our own unique persona and unique identity.
sentences.zh: 这样我们才能塑造出自己独特的个性和身份。

sentences.en: It is one of our goals, one of our missions as humans to go through this phase in our life.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，经历人生的这个阶段是我们的目标之一，也是我们的使命之一。

sentences.en: If you want to move from child to adult and then from adult to individual, you have to go through this period, maybe a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 如果你想从孩子变成成人，再从成人变成独立的个体，你就必须经历这个时期，也许还得经历几次。

sentences.en: And people who don't do this,
sentences.zh: 而那些没有这样做的人，

sentences.en: I think we all know one of them.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都认识这样的人。

sentences.en: They end up basically without an identity, very miserable.
sentences.zh: 他们最终基本上没有自我，非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And what this theory says is that they are incredibly malleable to others' opinions, others' expectations, and they go through life never really figuring out who they are.
sentences.zh: 这个理论认为，他们极易受他人观点、他人期望的影响，一生都从未真正弄清楚自己是谁。

sentences.en: That sounds pretty scary to me.
sentences.zh: 这听起来对我来说相当可怕。

sentences.en: Now, this word, individuation, very serious, might sound like a very serious term, but you have probably, if you are in your 20s, already experienced this to a degree.
sentences.zh: 现在，“个体化”这个词听起来可能非常严肃，但如果你正处于20多岁，你可能已经在一定程度上经历过这个过程了。

sentences.en: Even if you're like 18 or younger, that's when this really begins to take hold.
sentences.zh: 即使你才18岁或更小，那也是这个过程真正开始扎根的时候。

sentences.en: It's when we decide, you know, hey, maybe I don't want to study law at university just because my parents expect me to.
sentences.zh: 那是我们决定，你知道，嘿，也许我不想仅仅因为父母的期望而在大学学习法律。

sentences.en: Maybe I don't fully believe my family's ultra-conservative viewpoints.
sentences.zh: 也许我并不完全相信我家人的极端保守观点。

sentences.en: Maybe I don't like dressing this way.
sentences.zh: 也许我不喜欢这样穿衣。

sentences.en: Maybe this is more my personal style.
sentences.zh: 也许这才是我的个人风格。

sentences.en: We realize, maybe I don't like being around these people.
sentences.zh: 我们意识到，也许我不喜欢和这些人在一起。

sentences.en: Maybe I don't like my hometown.
sentences.zh: 也许我不喜欢我的家乡。

sentences.en: Maybe I don't want to have kids.
sentences.zh: 也许我不想生孩子。

sentences.en: Maybe I do want to have kids.
sentences.zh: 也许我确实想生孩子。

sentences.en: After saying that you thought one thing for a long time, and maybe now you feel differently about those matters.
sentences.zh: 在坚持了很久某种想法之后，也许现在你对这些事情有了不同的感受。

sentences.en: Our 20s are a period where we change our mind a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 20多岁是我们改变主意非常频繁的时期。

sentences.en: And we have a lot of these sort of, what we would call, epiphanies.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多这种所谓的“顿悟”。

sentences.en: These, like, come-to moments where we're like, wait, what am I doing?
sentences.zh: 这些“突然醒悟”的时刻，让我们觉得：等等，我在做什么？

sentences.en: Like, I don't like this.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I don't believe this.
sentences.zh: 我不相信这个。

sentences.en: I am not this.
sentences.zh: 我不是这样的人。

sentences.en: Firstly, it's because we gain a lot of independence, physically, but also emotionally.
sentences.zh: 首先，这是因为我们获得了很大的独立性，不仅是身体上的，还有情感上的。

sentences.en: But secondly, we are undergoing rapid identity development and experimentation.
sentences.zh: 但其次，我们正在经历快速的身份发展和实验。

sentences.en: You may find yourself wanting different things every three months, every year, every week, maybe.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现自己每三个月、每年，甚至每周都想要不同的东西。

sentences.en: That's actually totally normal.
sentences.zh: 这其实完全正常。

sentences.en: You know, one day you might feel like, oh, I need to leave this city and never come back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一天你可能会觉得，哦，我需要离开这个城市，永远不要回来。

sentences.en: I'm going to move to Puerto Rico.
sentences.zh: 我要搬到波多黎各。

sentences.en: I'm going to move to London.
sentences.zh: 我要搬到伦敦。

sentences.en: And then the next, you're like, no, I'm going to find a really nice person and settle down.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天，你会想，不，我要找一个很好的人安定下来。

sentences.en: Or I'm going to start a farm.
sentences.zh: 或者我要去开个农场。

sentences.en: And then the next, you're thinking,
sentences.zh: 然后下一刻，你在想，

sentences.en: I'm going to go back to university and I'm going to learn a trade.
sentences.zh: 我要回大学去学一门手艺。

sentences.en: And it's like a freaking cyclone in your mind of possibilities.
sentences.zh: 你的脑子里就像有一场疯狂的可能性旋风。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: That's actually exactly where you should be.
sentences.zh: 这其实正是你应该处在的状态。

sentences.en: I don't know if anyone's ever told you this, but that is, you're doing it right.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有没有人告诉过你，但这就是，你做得对。

sentences.en: You may have heard this idea that our brains aren't fully developed until 25.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过大脑要到25岁才完全发育成熟的说法。

sentences.en: I think that's a very famous, a famous fact that is actually a myth that is actually not entirely true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常著名的事实，但实际上是一个神话，并不完全正确。

sentences.en: And there's actually no solid evidence for this.
sentences.zh: 实际上并没有确凿的证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: Our brains continue to develop across our lifespan.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑在整个生命周期中都在持续发育。

sentences.en: They actually peak in maturation anywhere between 20 to our early 30s.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上在20岁到30岁出头之间的任何时候达到成熟的顶峰。

sentences.en: It's like, it's a very broad and individual process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常广泛且因人而异的过程。

sentences.en: I think the reason we hear 25 is because 25 just sounds like a fun number.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们听到25岁这个数字，是因为25听起来像是一个有趣的数字。

sentences.en: So our brains aren't fully developed at 25, but this is a period where we are doing a lot of fine tuning, especially in the prefrontal cortex,
sentences.zh: 所以我们的大脑在25岁时并没有完全发育成熟，但这是一个我们进行大量微调的时期，尤其是在前额叶皮层，

sentences.en: which this place, this part of our brain, it governs planning, it governs decision-making, it governs things like impulse control.
sentences.zh: 这个大脑部位掌管着规划、决策，以及冲动控制等功能。

sentences.en: And so with this ongoing development, that means that our sense of judgment, our priorities, our long-term thinking is still under construction.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着这种持续的发展，意味着我们的判断力、优先级、长期思考能力仍在构建中。

sentences.en: It is still shifting constantly.
sentences.zh: 它仍在不断变化。

sentences.en: And we also, just because of our age, have more doors open to us than we probably ever will.
sentences.zh: 而且，仅仅因为我们的年龄，我们面前敞开的大门比我们以后任何时候都要多。

sentences.en: In our teen years, you know, we are kind of limited by our age.
sentences.zh: 在十几岁的时候，你知道，我们受到年龄的限制。

sentences.en: We're kind of limited by our maturity.
sentences.zh: 我们受到成熟度的限制。

sentences.en: As we get older, we also become limited by past decisions that we made in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，我们也会受到20多岁时所做决定的限制。

sentences.en: You know, the decision to have kids, the decision to settle down in a certain place, the decision to get a mortgage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，生孩子的决定、在某个地方安定下来的决定、背负抵押贷款的决定。

sentences.en: So this is like the most perfect little space
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个最完美的空间，

sentences.en: and like nugget of time where our choices are so abundant.
sentences.zh: 也是一段最宝贵的时间，我们的选择如此丰富。

sentences.en: We're young, we're hopefully healthy, and we're like a kid in a candy store rushing about being like, no, I want this one.
sentences.zh: 我们年轻，希望我们健康，就像糖果店里的孩子一样，匆忙地跑来跑去说：“不，我要这个。”

sentences.en: No, I want this one.
sentences.zh: “不，我要那个。”

sentences.en: I want this life.
sentences.zh: “我想要这种生活。”

sentences.en: I want this life.
sentences.zh: “我想要那种生活。”

sentences.en: We can't choose.
sentences.zh: 我们无法抉择。

sentences.en: It's why we make plans for the future, maybe like six months out.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们为未来做计划，也许是六个月后的计划。

sentences.en: And then like, because we are changing so rapidly during this decade, by the time we get there, we've like already changed our minds again.
sentences.zh: 然后，因为我们在这一十年里变化太快，当我们到达那个时间点时，我们已经又改变主意了。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean you were lying about that choice or that that wasn't a priority at some stage.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你在那个选择上撒了谎，或者它在某个阶段不是优先事项。

sentences.en: It is literally just that the fact, like our,
sentences.zh: 事实仅仅是，就像我们的，

sentences.en: the rate at which we are changing as individuals outpaces the rate at which that we can sometimes make decisions and follow through on them.
sentences.zh: 我们作为个体改变的速度，有时超过了我们做出决定并执行它们的速度。

sentences.en: It is literally that you become a different person psychologically.
sentences.zh: 这真的是因为你在心理上变成了一个不同的人。

sentences.en: I think in our 20s, like every six months.
sentences.zh: 我认为在20多岁时，大约每六个月就会这样。

sentences.en: And I think that's important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点很重要。

sentences.en: This is quite literally the definition of trial and error.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是“摸着石头过河”的定义。

sentences.en: And I've said it before, I will continue to say it.
sentences.zh: 我以前说过，以后还会继续说。

sentences.en: Life is not meant to be a recipe where step one naturally leads into step two and step three until you've made the dish you decided on at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 人生不应该是一份食谱，第一步自然而然地引向第二步、第三步，直到你做出了最初决定的那道菜。

sentences.en: It is a series of experiments.
sentences.zh: 人生是一系列实验。

sentences.en: And even the experiments that don't work out, even the ones that you change your mind about, have taught you something.
sentences.zh: 即使是那些没有成功的实验，即使是那些让你改变主意的实验，也都教会了你一些东西。

sentences.en: I think in your 20s, you live many, many lives, or at least you should.
sentences.zh: 我认为在二十多岁的时候，你经历着许多许多种人生，或者至少你应该这样。

sentences.en: And changing your mind, being able to interpret what you want in a specific moment, even if that's different from what you wanted before,
sentences.zh: 而改变主意，能够解读自己在特定时刻想要什么，即使这与你之前想要的不同，

sentences.en: is a really, really important part of that.
sentences.zh: 这真的是非常、非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And it means that when you get to, your 30s or your 40s and you're ready to choose, you have as much information as you need to make the right choice.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当你到了三十多岁或四十多岁，准备好做出选择时，你已经拥有了做出正确选择所需的所有信息。

sentences.en: Now, these decisions, they often require action though, or at the very least, like some kind of vocalization.
sentences.zh: 不过，这些决定往往需要采取行动，或者至少需要某种形式的表达。

sentences.en: And this is where we find it hard to admit, I have changed my mind.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们难以承认的地方：我改变主意了。

sentences.en: I'm not that person anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不再是那个人了。

sentences.en: Especially if we've already kind of started down the path.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当我们已经踏上某条道路之后。

sentences.en: We think that just because we've said we are one thing, we must always be that thing.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，仅仅因为我们曾经说过自己是某种人，我们就必须永远是那种人。

sentences.en: We must always believe in what we once did with conviction.
sentences.zh: 我们必须始终坚信我们曾经深信不疑的东西。

sentences.en: We must always want what we claimed we once wanted.
sentences.zh: 我们必须始终想要我们曾经声称想要的东西。

sentences.en: Why do we think that?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么会这么想？

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Of course, it's not one reason.
sentences.zh: 当然，原因不止一个。

sentences.en: It's never one reason.
sentences.zh: 从来都不止一个原因。

sentences.en: It's a multitude of reasons.
sentences.zh: 原因有很多。

sentences.en: I think we don't always want to admit we've changed our mind because there is a great deal of cultural messaging to do with sticking things out, not quitting, following through,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们并不总是愿意承认自己改变了主意，因为文化中充斥着关于坚持到底、不轻言放弃、贯彻始终的信息，

sentences.en: finishing what you've started, being reliable, being trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 做完你开始的事，做一个可靠、值得信赖的人。

sentences.en: The driver behind this is really other people's desire
sentences.zh: 这背后的驱动力其实是其他人希望

sentences.en: for continuity from us.
sentences.zh: 我们保持连贯性。

sentences.en: They want us to be the same person that we were a year ago and a year before that so that they can understand us.
sentences.zh: 他们希望我们还是那个一年前、两年前的自己，这样他们才能理解我们。

sentences.en: And it's also this idea that, you know, being a hard worker and having follow through
sentences.zh: 而且还有一种观念，就是做一个努力工作、有始有终的人，

sentences.en: gives you some kind of like moral superiority or means that you have a better kind of character.
sentences.zh: 会给你带来某种道德上的优越感，或者意味着你拥有更好的品格。

sentences.en: The problem with this framing is that, yes, making promises to other people and making promises to yourself and following through is amazing and should be something
sentences.zh: 这种框架的问题在于，是的，对他人做出承诺，对自己做出承诺并贯彻始终，这很棒，也应该是你

sentences.en: that you aspire to do.
sentences.zh: 渴望去做的事情。

sentences.en: Not if, though, you don't actually want to do that thing.
sentences.zh: 但前提是你真的想做那件事。

sentences.en: We frame this as a failure of willpower that someone just didn't have what it took or just wasn't committed enough rather than realizing that changing your mind about these things
sentences.zh: 我们把这归结为意志力的失败，认为某人只是没有能力或不够坚定，而不是意识到改变主意

sentences.en: is actually a really natural developmental process and a really important sign of growth.
sentences.zh: 实际上是一个非常自然的发展过程，也是一个非常重要的成长标志。

sentences.en: But I think that framing is why we feel a lot of shame around, you know, maybe quitting a degree that wasn't right for us or stepping away from a venture
sentences.zh: 但我认为正是这种框架导致我们感到羞愧，比如放弃了一个不适合我们的学位，或者离开了一个项目，

sentences.en: or ending a long-term relationship, whatever it may be that we'd previously committed to because we think it means we don't have a follow-through.
sentences.zh: 或者结束了一段长期关系，无论我们之前承诺过什么，因为我们认为这意味着我们没有贯彻到底。

sentences.en: We think that it signals that we are a quitter rather than someone who is actually very, very brave.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这标志着我们是个半途而废的人，而不是一个实际上非常、非常勇敢的人。

sentences.en: This cultural conditioning, it is very powerful.
sentences.zh: 这种文化制约是非常强大的。

sentences.en: Sometimes, you know,
sentences.zh: 有时候，你知道，

sentences.en: I often have this thought where I think, like, I wonder how many people are in loveless marriages or are in careers they don't want or stuck in cities they don't actually like
sentences.zh: 我经常会有这样的想法：我想知道有多少人身处无爱的婚姻中，或者从事着他们并不想要的工作，或者困在他们并不喜欢的城市里，

sentences.en: or because they don't want to be seen as quitting or they don't want to be labelled as unreliable.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为他们不想被视为半途而废，或者不想被贴上不可靠的标签。

sentences.en: And how wild is it that we have prioritised the opinions of
sentences.zh: 我们竟然把某些人的意见看得比我们自己的欲望还重要，

sentences.en: some people that we may not even know or the opinions of people who don't actually have to live our life
sentences.zh: 这些人我们甚至可能都不认识，或者他们根本不需要过我们的生活，

sentences.en: over our own desires?
sentences.zh: 这难道不疯狂吗？

sentences.en: Like, it's really strange
sentences.zh: 这真的很奇怪，

sentences.en: that we do that to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们竟然对自己做这种事。

sentences.en: This kind of brings me to the next big factor and that is the fear of judgement.
sentences.zh: 这让我引出了下一个大因素，那就是对评判的恐惧。

sentences.en: Mainly, the fear of disappointing people as we just said, especially people who are close to us.
sentences.zh: 主要是害怕让别人失望，正如我们刚才所说的，尤其是那些与我们亲近的人。

sentences.en: For many of us in our 20s,
sentences.zh: 对于我们许多二十多岁的人来说，

sentences.en: let's just say it, I think that's our parents.
sentences.zh: 直说吧，我认为那就是我们的父母。

sentences.en: And our fear of disappointing our parents isn't one-dimensional, it's actually very complex.
sentences.zh: 我们害怕让父母失望，这种恐惧不是单一维度的，实际上非常复杂。

sentences.en: For starters, your parents may have placed a lot of expectation on you that ended up really controlling your life.
sentences.zh: 首先，你的父母可能对你寄予了厚望，最终导致他们控制了你的生活。

sentences.en: I know this is particularly the experience for firstborns, for eldest daughters, the children of immigrants, for example, the children of high achievers.
sentences.zh: 我知道这对于长子长女、移民子女，或者高成就者的子女来说，尤其如此。

sentences.en: I'm not an immigrant so I can't directly speak to that experience but it's something I get a lot of DMs about.
sentences.zh: 我不是移民，所以我不能直接谈论那种经历，但这确实是我经常收到的私信内容。

sentences.en: How can I let my parents down?
sentences.zh: 我怎么能让父母失望呢？

sentences.en: How can I forge my own path?
sentences.zh: 我怎么能开辟自己的道路呢？

sentences.en: How can I make them value my interests even if they aren't going to make a whole lot of money when they have sacrificed so much to get me here?
sentences.zh: 当他们为了让我来到这里、为了抚养我、为了给我更好的生活而牺牲了那么多时，我怎么能让他们重视我的兴趣，即使这些兴趣赚不到什么钱？

sentences.en: So much to get me to this place, to raise me, to give me a better life.
sentences.zh: 为了让我达到这个位置，为了抚养我，为了给我更好的生活，他们牺牲了太多。

sentences.en: There was a 2020 study that found that the children of first-generation immigrants often experience
sentences.zh: 2020年的一项研究发现，第一代移民的子女在满足父母的学业期望方面，

sentences.en: significantly more stress compared to their peers when it comes to meeting their parents' academic expectations.
sentences.zh: 往往比同龄人承受更大的压力。

sentences.en: In fact, they often cite it as one of their main forms of academic motivation to please their parents, to live out their parents' dream compared to non-immigrant children
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们经常提到这是他们主要的学习动力之一：取悦父母，实现父母的梦想，这与非移民子女相比，

sentences.en: who say that often what motivates their study is a sense of personal achievement or some kind of personal goal.
sentences.zh: 非移民子女通常说他们的学习动力来自于个人成就感或某种个人目标。

sentences.en: They worry a lot less about parental approval, especially again for firstborns.
sentences.zh: 他们对父母的认可担忧要少得多，尤其是长子长女。

sentences.en: Imagine if you are a firstborn, first-generation immigrant oh my god, the pressure to not let down your parents must be astounding.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果你是长子，又是第一代移民，天哪，那种不能让父母失望的压力一定是惊人的。

sentences.en: And birth order theory, whether you believe it or not, does hypothesize that if you are the firstborn child, the standard for you is higher.
sentences.zh: 而且出生顺序理论，无论你是否相信，确实假设如果你是长子，你的标准会更高。

sentences.en: The expectations are greater.
sentences.zh: 期望值更高。

sentences.en: You are the example.
sentences.zh: 你是榜样。

sentences.en: You are being molded to eventually become the guide and the leader for the family.
sentences.zh: 你被塑造为最终成为家庭的向导和领导者。

sentences.en: So stepping away from the dream your parents have for you, that's going against decades in some cases of validation and decades of training.
sentences.zh: 所以，背离父母为你设定的梦想，在某些情况下，这违背了数十年的认可和数十年的训练。

sentences.en: You know, if you're 20,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你20岁，

sentences.en: 21, 27, whatever it is, that's like
sentences.zh: 21岁，27岁，无论多少岁，那就像是

sentences.en: 20 years that this is the information you have been receiving from those around you to please them, to impress them, to do what is best according to them.

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题是这样的。

sentences.en: You have two options here.
sentences.zh: 你在这里有两个选择。

sentences.en: You can keep up the facade.
sentences.zh: 你可以继续维持这种假象。

sentences.en: You can keep up with the expectations.
sentences.zh: 你可以继续满足这些期望。

sentences.en: You can keep up with what other people want from you.
sentences.zh: 你可以继续做别人想要你做的事。

sentences.en: But that is a choice.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种选择。

sentences.zh: 你确实有选择权。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you some hard love here.
sentences.zh: 我要对你说些逆耳忠言。

sentences.en: At some stage, you have decided that this is what you are going to do.
sentences.zh: 在某个阶段，你已经决定了这就是你要做的事情。

sentences.en: Even if you didn't realize it, you have decided to suppress the deeper individualized version of you.
sentences.zh: 即使你没有意识到，你也已经决定压抑那个更深层的、个性化的自我。

sentences.en: And that might be because it is the right choice based on your priorities.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为根据你的优先事项，这是正确的选择。

sentences.en: If disappointing your parents or letting them down is more serious to you than choosing your own path, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 如果让父母失望对你来说比选择自己的道路更严重，那没关系。

sentences.zh: 你已经做出了那个选择。

sentences.zh: 但我只是想提醒你，改变主意也是一种选择。

sentences.zh: 这需要极大的勇气，但在失望的另一面是清晰和成长。

sentences.zh: 不打破几个鸡蛋，就做不成煎蛋卷。

sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你刻薄。

sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为不让别人失望，实际上意味着你对自己真的很刻薄。

sentences.en: It's actually a profound form of honesty and multiple studies including a very famous one from the University of Chicago find that actually

sentences.en: being honest about your preferences, being willing to say no or to say
